objects_built.name: require_manager
objects_built.role: Loads the caller's role from users by user_id and stops with a precondition unless it is manager or admin. Called first by refund approval and price changes.

objects_changed.change: Added function.run require_manager with user_id $auth.id as the first statement.

objects_changed.change: Added function.run require_manager with user_id $auth.id as the first statement.

templates_considered: AUTH-030: fit. Users can't make themselves admin; covers role writes from input. Used as-is with fields [role].
AUTH-002: did not fit. Its selector is admin paths or the admin tag, and this ask is about specific write endpoints, not admin paths.
AUTH-020 and the other access templates: did not fit. They concern record ownership, not role gating.

rules.covers: nobody can give themselves manager by writing role from request input
only managers can approve refunds or change prices; the two endpoints call the role check first with the logged-in user

ask_parts_not_covered.part: regular staff can view but not change, beyond the refund approve and price endpoints
ask_parts_not_covered.why: other is a scope question: no single check says which writes are manager-only; needs the customer to name them

ask_parts_not_covered.part: AI tool issue_refund can issue Stripe refunds with no role check
ask_parts_not_covered.why: other: left out of the plan; the customer has not said whether it should require a manager

ask_parts_not_covered.part: which roles count as manager (admin included?)
ask_parts_not_covered.why: couldn't tell: the ask says managers, the workspace has admin and manager roles

ask_parts_not_covered.part: who holds the manager role and how it is granted

ask_parts_not_covered.part: runtime enforcement and stored role values
ask_parts_not_covered.why: needs runtime/org process: checks read definitions only

assumptions: The users.role enum (admin, support_lead, manager, staff, member, viewer) is the role vocabulary; 'manager' is the enum value.
admin should pass the manager check (the plan allows both manager and admin).
The approve and price endpoints are the only refund-approval and price-change paths in scope.
The signup endpoint does not set role, so new users get the default member role.
confusions: The skill says a rule warning that a function does not exist means the rule judges nothing, but a function built in the same change is expected to be missing until push. The parse warning for ACCESS-MGR-001.R1 appeared for that reason; the skill does not say whether a new object in the same change clears this before push. Had to judge it expected.

The skill's Build recipe for 'Keep admin endpoints for admins' uses a require_role function with a db.get on the user table; the same shape worked for require_manager, but the recipe is about admin paths, not per-endpoint write gating, and I had to adapt it.
The skill's statement.expression_rule and precondition shapes are not in the catalogue; I used the workspace's login_POST precondition syntax as the reference for the role precondition.
wished_for: A template or recipe for 'only role X may call these specific endpoints': this is different from admin-path gating and needs a function plus statement_required scoped by endpoint names.
A way for the parser to accept a function that is being built in the same change without a warning, or a note on whether the rule is judged after push.
Guidance on whether 'staff view only' should be enforced by listing write endpoints, or by a different mechanism.
why_confidence: Both gates are wired in the dry run's preview (the function, the two endpoints and the role-write fix), and the statement_required rule names the function and the endpoints. Confidence is only medium because the 'staff view only' part is covered for two endpoints, not for every write; the AI refund tool bypasses the role check; and admin passing is an assumption. Policy evaluation has not been run, so no finding has been observed.
